1.reason: politician is the only standard spelling; the other three are misspellings.

2.reason: Languages (Spanish) and numbered course titles (Algebra I) are capitalized; 'algebra I' with a capital numeral is not accepted by school grammars.

3.reason: Short prepositions ('of') stay lowercase in document titles under AP, Chicago and MLA.

4.reason: development drops the e of develop before -ment, with a single l; no dictionary accepts the others.

5.reason: veterinarian is the only accepted spelling.

6.reason: professional is the only accepted spelling (one f, ss, -ional).

7.reason: hazardous is the only accepted spelling (hazard plus -ous).

8.reason: 'resturant' misspells restaurant; hygiene, guarantee and schedule are correct.

9.reason: suspicious is the only accepted spelling.

10.reason: 'concious' misspells conscious; nuisance, achievement and fiery are correct.

11.reason: AP, Chicago and MLA all capitalize verbs (Is) and pronouns (It) in titles regardless of length.

12.reason: 'mischeif' misspells mischief; vacuum, receipt and pursue are correct.

13.reason: Middle Ages is a capitalized period name; 'medieval' is a lowercase adjective under Chicago, AP and MLA.

14.reason: compromise is -ise in both US and British spelling, so the -ize options are not regional variants.

15.reason: acquitted has cq and a doubled t before -ed (final stressed syllable); no dictionary accepts the others.

16.reason: cemetery is the only accepted spelling.

17.reason: accidentally (accidental plus -ly) is the only accepted spelling.

18.reason: Named wars (Revolutionary War) and treaties (Treaty of Paris) are proper nouns; the later generic 'the war' is correctly lowercase.

19.reason: A compass direction (south) and a descriptive 'eastern coast' are lowercase; only a region name like Midwest (or East Coast) is capitalized.

20.reason: millionaire is the only accepted spelling.

21.reason: accelerate (cc, single l) is the only accepted spelling.

22.reason: 'questionaire' misspells questionnaire; liaison, fluorescent and perseverance are correct.

23.reason: 'exagerrate' misspells exaggerate; possession, discipline and colleague are correct.

24.reason: A generic title before a name ('a senator') and a common noun ('a bill') are lowercase; the Senate as a named body is capitalized.

25.reason: 'villian' misspells villain; circuit, biscuit and ancient are correct.

26.reason: mortgage is the only accepted spelling.

27.reason: 'occured' misspells occurred; lowercase 'parliament' in a generic use is acceptable, so D is not an error.

28.reason: permanent is the only accepted spelling.

29.reason: indispensable is standard; 'indispensible' survives only as an archaic or obsolete variant in historical dictionaries and is marked as an error in current US and British usage.

30.reason: comparison is the only accepted spelling.

31.reason: 'silouette' misspells silhouette; conscientious, acquaintance and millennium are correct.

32.reason: Each quotation is a complete sentence introduced by a dialogue tag, so each begins with a capital.

33.reason: 'foriegn' misspells foreign; scissors, solemn and souvenir are correct.

34.reason: sacrifice is the only accepted spelling (no -ise variant exists in British spelling for this word).

35.reason: pronunciation drops the o of pronounce; 'pronounciation' is a common error, not a variant.

36.reason: height is the standard spelling; 'heighth' appears in some dictionaries only as dialectal or nonstandard, which is not an accepted written form.
